answers.working:
The **cockroach** (an arthropod) has an **open circulatory system**: haemolymph flows out of the vessels into open spaces called sinuses. Its excretory organs are the **Malpighian tubules**. So 1, 4 and 6 go together.

The **earthworm** (an annelid) has a **closed circulatory system**, where blood always stays inside vessels, and it excretes through **nephridia**. So 2, 3 and 5 go together.

Option (A) wrongly puts the earthworm with an open system, and options (C) and (D) mix up the excretory organs. So the answer is option (B).

answers.value: Plant A turns redder than Plant B.
answers.working:
Water rises up the xylem mainly because of the **transpiration pull**: water evaporating from the leaves pulls the water column up from the roots.

In very dry air the difference in water vapour between the leaf and the air is large, so plant A transpires fast and pulls up a lot of dyed water. In high humidity the air is already nearly saturated, so plant B transpires slowly and draws up much less dye.

So plant A will carry more dye into its stem and leaves and turn redder. So the answer is option (A).

answers.label: D
answers.working:
This is **natural selection** of the kind Darwin saw in the Galapagos finches. Beaks in a population vary a little. Once the medium seeds are gone, only large seeds are left as food.

Birds whose beaks happen to be on the larger side can crack large seeds, so they survive better and leave more offspring. Over generations the average beak size of the population shifts upwards (directional selection).

The beaks will not stay unchanged, because selection now favours one end of the range, and smaller beaks would be a disadvantage. Extinction is not the most likely outcome, since food is still available. So the answer is option (D).

answers.label: D
answers.working:
With limited food and housing, the population follows **logistic growth**:

\(\dfrac{dN}{dt} = rN\left(\dfrac{K - N}{K}\right)\)

Here \(r = 0.1\), the present population \(N = 100\) and the carrying capacity \(K = 200\).

\(\dfrac{dN}{dt} = 0.1 \times 100 \times \dfrac{200 - 100}{200} = 10 \times 0.5 = 5\) people per year.

Without the limit (exponential growth) the rate would be \(rN = 10\) per year; the factor \(\dfrac{K-N}{K}\) halves it. So the answer is option (D).

answers.label: A
answers.value: The inner and outer membranes have identical sets of enzymes.
answers.working:
The two membranes of a mitochondrion are very different. The **inner membrane** carries the electron transport chain and ATP synthase, while the **outer membrane** is a porous, simpler membrane. Their enzymes are not the same, so statement (A) is incorrect.

The other statements are true: the matrix holds a single circular DNA molecule and 70S ribosomes, and the inner membrane folds into **cristae** to increase its surface area.

So the answer is option (A).

answers.label: B
answers.value: Cells in this stage are metabolically active but not dividing.
answers.working:
Some cells leave the cycle after the G1 phase and enter an inactive stage called **quiescent stage (G0)**. Such cells stay **metabolically active** (they carry out their normal functions) but they **do not proliferate**, unless they are called on to do so. Mature nerve cells are a common example.

They are not dying, and they are not dividing, which rules out the other options. So the answer is option (B).

answers.label: D
answers.value: Administering anti-Rh antibodies to a Rh -ve mother after her first Rh +ve child birth.
answers.working:
**Erythroblastosis foetalis** happens when an **Rh negative** mother carries an **Rh positive** foetus. During the first delivery some foetal Rh+ blood enters the mother, and she starts making anti-Rh antibodies. In the next pregnancy these antibodies cross the placenta and destroy the red blood cells of an Rh+ foetus.

To prevent this, the mother is given **anti-Rh antibodies** right after the delivery of her first Rh+ child. They clear the foetal Rh+ cells before her own immune system can respond, so she does not become sensitised.

An Rh+ woman never makes anti-Rh antibodies, so options (A) and (B) are irrelevant, and giving them before the first pregnancy (C) does not target the moment the foetal cells enter. So the answer is option (D).

answers.label: C
answers.working:
In the electron transport chain, electrons from NADH and \(\mathrm{FADH_2}\) pass through complexes I to IV. Cytochrome c is only a carrier between complex III and complex IV.

At complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase) the electrons are finally handed to **oxygen**, which combines with protons to form water: \(\mathrm{O_2 + 4H^+ + 4e^- \rightarrow 2H_2O}\). Oxygen is therefore the **terminal electron acceptor**.

\(\mathrm{NAD^+}\) and FAD accept electrons earlier, in glycolysis and the Krebs cycle, not at the end of the chain. So the answer is option (C).

answers.label: D
answers.working:
Immature lymphocytes develop into mature, antigen-sensitive lymphocytes in the **primary lymphoid organs**: the bone marrow and the **thymus**. T lymphocytes mature in the thymus.

The spleen and Peyer's patches are **secondary lymphoid organs**, where already mature lymphocytes meet antigens and multiply. The liver is not a lymphoid organ.

Of the choices, only the thymus is a primary lymphoid organ. So the answer is option (D).

answers.label: C
answers.value: \(K_M\) is the concentration of substrate when the velocity of the reaction is half that of the maximal velocity.
answers.working:
Put \(V_0 = \dfrac{V_{max}}{2}\) into the equation:

\(\dfrac{V_{max}}{2} = V_{max} \cdot \dfrac{[S]}{K_M + [S]}\)

so \(K_M + [S] = 2[S]\), which gives \([S] = K_M\).

So \(K_M\) is the **substrate concentration** at which the reaction runs at half its maximum velocity. It has units of concentration, not velocity, and it does not describe the enzyme's concentration or any optimum pH or temperature. So the answer is option (C).

answers.label: D
answers.value: Adequate rest and a balanced diet for at least three days.
answers.working:
The common cold is a **viral** infection. **Antibiotics** such as streptomycin and amoxycillin act on bacteria (for example on their cell wall or 70S ribosomes) and have no effect on viruses, so options (A), (B) and (C) do not treat the cause. Using them needlessly also helps bacteria become resistant.

A cold is self-limiting: the body's own immune system clears the rhinovirus in a few days. Rest and a balanced diet support that immune response.

So the answer is option (D).

answers.label: B
answers.working:
In human females, **oogenesis begins in the foetus**. During embryonic development, millions of oogonia form in each foetal ovary, and they enter meiosis I and stop at prophase I as **primary oocytes**. No new oogonia are made after birth.

At puberty these primary oocytes start maturing, and ovulation releases a secondary oocyte, but these are later stages of a process that has already started. So the answer is option (B).

answers.label: A
answers.value: It is multilayered and mainly protects from chemical and mechanical stresses.
answers.working:
A **compound epithelium** is made of more than one layer of cells (multilayered). Because of this it has only a limited role in secretion and absorption; its **main function is protection** against chemical and mechanical stresses. It covers the dry surface of the skin, the moist lining of the buccal cavity and pharynx, and the inner lining of the ducts of salivary glands and the pancreatic duct.

Binding tissues together is the job of connective tissue, and active secretion and absorption are the jobs of simple and glandular epithelia. So the answer is option (A).

answers.label: D
answers.working:
In snapdragon, red (RR) crossed with white (rr) gives pink (Rr) in F1, because neither allele is fully dominant (**incomplete dominance**).

Selfing the pink F1 (Rr x Rr) gives genotypes RR : Rr : rr in the ratio **1 : 2 : 1**.

Since the heterozygote has its own colour, each genotype shows a different phenotype: red : pink : white = **1 : 2 : 1**. So both ratios are 1:2:1, unlike complete dominance where the phenotype ratio would be 3:1. So the answer is option (D).

answers.label: A
answers.value: All three RE1, RE2 and RE3 digested DNA.
answers.working:
Two cut ends can be joined by DNA ligase if their **sticky ends** (single-stranded overhangs) are complementary.

Each enzyme cuts the top strand between the 1st and 2nd base and the bottom strand between the 5th and 6th base (reading the top strand left to right). So every cut leaves a four-base overhang made of bases 2 to 5 of the top strand:

| Enzyme | Site (top strand) | Overhang |
|---|---|---|
| RE1 | AAGCTT | AGCT |
| RE2 | CAGCTG | AGCT |
| RE3 | GAGCTC | AGCT |

All three enzymes leave the same AGCT overhang (which is its own complement read in the opposite direction), even though their full recognition sites differ. So an RE1 sticky end can pair with, and be ligated to, DNA cut by RE1, RE2 or RE3. So the answer is option (A).
